private_notes.observations: No prior panel rates or hour allocations are available. Our fully loaded cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive rate that leaves a meaningful margin. Use subsequent published rate cards and allocated hours to assess how sensitive demand is to price, then adjust for long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, a $300 rate yielded 445 hours and $44,450 profit despite both other firms charging $274. One quarter is insufficient to estimate how strongly hours respond to rate changes.
private_notes.plan: Lower the rate modestly to test whether a narrower price gap increases allocated hours enough to offset the smaller margin. Compare Q2 hours and the next published rate card before making a larger adjustment.

private_notes.observations: At $300 in Q1, we received 445 hours; at $295 in Q2, we received 480 hours. Both competitors held their rates at $274. The $5 reduction coincided with higher hours and slightly higher profit, though two quarters are insufficient to establish a reliable demand curve.
private_notes.plan: Reduce the rate moderately to $285. This tests whether additional hours compensate for the lower margin without immediately matching competitors' $274 rates. Reassess after observing Q3 hours and the next rate card.

private_notes.observations: Reducing our rate from $300 to $285 increased allocated hours from 445 to 557 and quarterly profit from $44,450 to $47,322. Both competitors held at $274 throughout Q1–Q3.
private_notes.plan: Set $280 to test whether a modest further reduction increases total profit. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q3 before making another adjustment.

private_notes.observations: Reducing our rate from $300 to $280 increased allocated hours from 445 to 598 and quarterly profit from $44,450 to $47,822. Both other firms have held their rates at $274 throughout.
private_notes.plan: Test $275, just above the other firms' stable $274 rate. Compare the resulting profit with Q4 before lowering the rate further.

private_notes.observations: The other two firms have held at $274 throughout Q1–Q5. Lowering our rate from $300 to $275 steadily increased both allocated hours and quarterly profit; Q5 profit was $48,039, the highest yet.
private_notes.plan: Test matching the panel's $274 rate. Compare the resulting profit with Q5 before considering any further reduction; avoid a substantial cut given the declining margin per hour.

private_notes.observations: Both competing firms have held at $274 for six quarters. Our highest observed quarterly profit was at $274 in Q6 ($48,045), only slightly above the $48,039 earned at $275 in Q5.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $274. The evidence for further reductions is weak, and matching the stable panel rate preserves margin while maintaining a competitive allocation.

private_notes.observations: Both other firms have held at $274 for seven quarters. Our profit rose as we lowered our rate to $274, then remained at about $48,045 in Q7 with the same rate and allocation as Q6.
private_notes.plan: Hold at the matching panel rate. A further cut would sacrifice margin without evidence of enough additional hours to compensate; reassess if competitors change rates or allocation shifts.

private_notes.observations: Both other panel firms have held at $274 throughout. Matching $274 has yielded about 649 hours and $48,045 profit in each of the last three quarters, slightly above the observed profit at other tested rates.
private_notes.plan: Continue matching the stable panel rate. Reassess if competitors' rates or our allocated hours change.

private_notes.observations: Both other firms have held at $274 throughout nine quarters. Our highest observed quarterly profit is approximately $48,045 at $274; higher rates produced less profit. Hours and profit have been stable for four quarters at that rate.
private_notes.plan: Match the stable $274 panel rate this quarter. Reassess if competitors' rates or our allocation changes.

private_notes.observations: Both other firms have held at $274 for ten quarters. Our profit rose as we lowered our rate to $274 and has remained $48,045 per quarter for five quarters.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $274 while competitors and allocations remain stable. Reassess if the rate card or our allocated hours change.

private_notes.observations: At $274, allocated hours and quarterly profit have remained steady at 649 hours and $48,045 from Q6 through Q11. Both other panel firms have held their rates at $274 throughout.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $274 given the stable allocation and the highest observed quarterly profit at that rate. Reassess if competitor rates or allocated hours change.

private_notes.observations: Both competitors have held at $274 throughout all 12 quarters. Our $274 rate has produced a stable allocation of 649 hours and the highest reported quarterly profit, $48,045.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $274 while competitor rates and allocations remain stable; reassess if either changes.

private_notes.observations: Both competing firms have held their rates at $274 since Q2. Our $274 rate has consistently yielded 649 hours and approximately $48,045 in quarterly profit; tested higher rates yielded less profit.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $274 while competitor rates and allocations remain stable. Reassess if either changes.

private_notes.observations: Both other firms have held at $274 for 12 quarters. At our $274 rate, allocations and profit have remained stable at 649 hours and about $48,045 per quarter; higher rates earned less.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $274 while competitors' rates and our allocation remain stable. Reassess if either changes.

private_notes.observations: Both other firms have held at $274 since Q4. Matching them has delivered a stable allocation of about 649 hours and roughly $48,045 profit per quarter.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $274 while competitor rates and our allocation remain stable. Reassess if either changes.

private_notes.observations: All three panel firms have charged $274 since Q6. Our allocation has remained 649 hours, yielding approximately $48,045 profit per quarter.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $274 while rates and allocation remain stable. Reassess independently if either changes.

private_notes.observations: For 12 consecutive quarters, all three firms charged $274 and our allocation stayed at 649 hours. No new evidence suggests a different rate would improve long-run profit.
private_notes.plan: Maintain $274 this quarter. Reassess if panel rates or allocated hours change.

private_notes.observations: All three firms have charged $274 for at least 12 consecutive quarters; our allocation has remained 649 hours, yielding approximately $48,000 per quarter. No historical variation is shown to estimate Meridian’s response to a rate change.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest unilateral reduction to $273 to learn whether a lower rate earns enough additional hours to improve profit. Compare the resulting profit and panel rates next quarter before adjusting further.

private_notes.observations: At $273, 658 hours yielded $48,038 profit, $7 less than the $48,045 earned at $274 with 649 hours. Both other firms remained at $274.
private_notes.plan: Return to $274: the one-dollar reduction increased hours but did not improve profit. Continue assessing our own rate against realized hours and profit.
